sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use climbs above about 0.5.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk generally increases with it.
The effect of utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies: a high utilization adds much more risk for applicants who have delinquencies than for those who have none.
Income is among the third or fourth most important drivers, and risk decreases as income rises.
Length of credit history is also among the third or fourth most important drivers, and risk decreases as the history gets longer.
The debt-to-income ratio has at most a weak effect, and risk increases with it.
Age hardly matters. The data do not settle whether feature_a or feature_b affects default risk.
